meta.title: Online shop on AWS: trust boundaries and payment flow
meta.subtitle: Architecture review draft: shop-dev and shop-prod, with Stripe and Auth0
meta.source: Team's verbal description in the review request (no Terraform, console export or diagram was supplied)
meta.summary: Two AWS accounts, shop-dev and shop-prod, each with a VPC (public and private subnets), an ALB, an ECS Fargate service running the storefront and the orders API, RDS Postgres, Secrets Manager holding the Stripe key, and CloudWatch logs. Prod adds CloudFront with WAF in front of the ALB. The orders API calls Stripe through a NAT gateway. Customers log in with Auth0; the storefront validates the tokens Auth0 issues.
meta.issuesIntro: Measured against the usual review expectations: dev and prod use only their own resources, payment failures page someone, and internet-facing entry points are protected.
notes: Everything comes from one conversation. Chips say whether the team stated it or the modeller inferred it; the status 'Suspected, not confirmed' marks the team's own unconfirmed suspicion. Nothing here was checked against live config.
The dev-to-prod secret link is a team suspicion, not a confirmed fact. Turn on the Issues layer to see it.
Hops the team did not describe (ALB to storefront, storefront to orders API, orders API to RDS, orders API to Secrets Manager) are drawn as inferred links.

Not stated, worth asking: whether dev uses a separate Auth0 tenant and a Stripe test-mode key, which subnet RDS sits in, whether the dev ALB is internet-facing, and whether storefront and orders API are one ECS service or two.

issues.title: Dev orders API may read the prod Stripe key
records: Team: dev's orders API is thought to point at the prod Secrets Manager, because a task definition was copied. Not confirmed.
issues.cause: Team's hypothesis: the dev task definition was copied from prod and its secret ARN was not changed. Inference: a cross-account read only works if the prod secret's resource policy and its KMS key both allow shop-dev, so checking those also confirms or rules this out. If it is true, dev may be making live Stripe charges.
fix: Confirm: compare the secret ARNs in the dev orders API task definition with the shop-prod account
Confirm: search shop-prod CloudTrail for GetSecretValue calls from shop-dev principals
If confirmed: point dev at its own secret with a Stripe test-mode key, remove any cross-account grant, and rotate the prod Stripe key
Prevent: deny cross-account access in the prod secret's resource policy

issues.title: No alerting on payment failures
records: Team: there's no alerting on payment failures yet
fix: Log Stripe charge failures from the orders API in a consistent form
Add a CloudWatch metric filter and alarm on that log line, routed to an on-call channel
Name an owner for the alarm

issues.title: Dev ALB has no CloudFront or WAF in front
records: Prod has CloudFront and WAF in front of its ALB; dev does not
issues.cause: Not raised by the team. A public-subnet ALB without WAF is reachable from the internet unless something else restricts it, and dev may hold a prod secret (issue i1).
fix: Confirm whether the dev ALB is internet-facing
If it is, restrict it to the team's IP ranges or VPN, or add a WAF

steps.title: Online shop on AWS
steps.text: Two AWS accounts side by side (shop-prod, shop-dev), with Auth0 and customers on the left and Stripe on the right. Logs and alerting sit on the floor below. Chips on every item say whether the team stated it, suspects it, or it is inferred.

steps.title: 1. Trust boundaries
steps.text: Each account is its own trust boundary, and so is each vendor. Every line that crosses a box is a trust decision; click any line to see which boundaries it leaves and enters.

steps.title: 2. Customer login
steps.text: Customers log in with Auth0, which issues tokens the storefront validates. Not stated: whether dev and prod share one Auth0 tenant.

steps.title: 3. Into prod through the edge
steps.text: Customers reach prod through CloudFront, with WAF on the distribution, then the ALB in the public subnet. The hops past the ALB are inferred. Open question: can the ALB be reached directly, bypassing WAF?

steps.title: 4. Payment to Stripe
steps.text: The orders API reads the Stripe key from Secrets Manager (inferred) and calls Stripe out through the NAT gateway (stated). This is where payment data leaves the account.

steps.title: 5. Dev and the prod secret (suspected)
steps.text: The team thinks the dev orders API reads the prod Stripe key because its task definition was copied. That is unconfirmed; see issue i1 for how to check. If true, dev may be charging real cards.

steps.title: 6. No payment-failure alerting
steps.text: Logs reach CloudWatch, but nothing alerts when a payment fails (issue i2).

steps.title: 7. Dev edge
steps.text: Dev has no CloudFront or WAF. Whether its ALB is reachable from the internet is not stated (issue i3).
